newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X Minerals shrs climb in heavy trading.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X Minerals shrs climb in heavy trading.

text.p: Shares in Canadian gold prospector Bre-X Minerals Ltd rose on Thursday as the volatile stock resumed trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Bre-X's stock was up 0.13 at 3.33 in heavy midday turnover of 4.11 million shares on Canada's biggest stock market.

The stock fell 0.65 to 3.20 on massive turnover of 11.7 million shares on Wednesday before trading was halted in Toronto due to to a heavy volume of orders and technical problems with the exchange's computer trading system.
Bre-X has been hammered recently by doubts over the size and viability of its Busang gold discovery in Indonesia.

"There isn't enough news out there to tell you what is going on," said Kerry Smith, with First Marathon Securities Ltd. He said Bre-X may be getting a lift from published comments by Placer Dome Inc Chief Executive John Willson that he expected the Busang discovery to "pan out".

Bre-X has been under heavy fire since last week when its partner in Indonesia, Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc., revealed that early drilling samples performed during its due diligence process on the Busang gold property in the rain forests of Borneo turned up "insignificant" amounts of gold and "visual differences" from Bre-X's gold samples.
Placer Dome proposed a merger with Bre-X before the agreement with Freeport and Indonesian partners was struck earlier this year.

In an interview published in the Vancouver Sun newspaper, Willson said: "We basically said to ourselves -- we convinced ourselves -- that yes, it is (real). On the basis of the way (Bre-X's people) are behaving, the number of holes that have been drilled, the number of samples that had been taken, and the physical improbability of salting the samples," Willson said.
He added: "I would -- honest to God -- still be surprised if this (Busang) was not legitimate.
Willson speculated Freeport's poor test results from the Busang site may be due to its assaying and sampling methods.
"Sometimes it takes a long time to develop a good method of taking your core and preparing the samples and getting a reliable assay out of them," Willson said.
